useCases.title: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Clause 6.1 — Risk-assessment evidence: live risk register decay
useCases.value: Produces the evidence the external auditor expects at stage-2: proof that each risk line in the ISMS register was reviewed within its cadence, identifying exact owners of overdue entries.

useCases.title: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Annex A.5.24 — Incident-management planning: runbook currency attestation
useCases.value: Satisfies the A.5.24 'planning and preparation' sub-requirement: incident procedures are continuously refreshed, not one-time written.

useCases.title: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Annex A.5.25 — Event classification decisions: SIEM-to-incident triage traceability
useCases.value: Gives the Audit Committee a single number: 'classification SLA adherence %'. Analysts know their backlog, auditors see the proof.

useCases.title: SOC 2 CC6.7 — System boundary & data-transmission control: unapproved egress destinations
useCases.value: Provides the evidence SOC 2 auditors want: proof that outbound flows are governed and deviations are captured. Supports reduction of shadow SaaS risk.

useCases.title: SOC 2 CC7.1 — System-operations monitoring: uptime attestation and alert-noise governance
useCases.value: Lets the Head of IT Operations present the Audit Committee with coverage % (target 100% for production) and alert-noise % (target <5/day/CI). The same query replaces three spreadsheets.

useCases.title: SOC 2 CC7.3 — Evaluated events: threshold breaches without documented rationale
useCases.value: Gives leadership proof that events are not only closed but justifiably closed. Auditors consider an 'auto-closed without rationale' event a material weakness.

useCases.title: SOC 2 CC7.4 — Incident response: post-incident review completion SLA
useCases.value: Surfaces PIR backlog before it becomes an audit finding. Board sees a rolling '% of PIRs on time' metric.

useCases.title: SOC 2 CC9.1 — Risk-mitigation activity: vendor-risk action closure SLA
useCases.value: Replaces the quarterly Procurement PowerPoint with a continuous signal. Top vendors with overdue actions are the first line of an Audit Committee brief.

useCases.title: PCI-DSS 8.4 — MFA coverage: administrative access to CDE without MFA

useCases.title: PCI-DSS 11.3 — Vulnerability programme: overdue scan cadence and unremediated high-severity
useCases.value: Closes the #1 open-finding reason at QSAs — 'the scan history was incomplete'. Continuous measurement is the intended replacement.

useCases.title: PCI-DSS 12.10 — Incident response: IR readiness — playbook exercise evidence
useCases.value: Converts the 'we did a tabletop' email into indexed evidence auditors can query directly.

useCases.title: PCI-DSS 12.3 — Targeted risk analysis: frequency adherence for per-requirement TRAs
useCases.value: Gives compliance an explicit overdue list — the v4.0 TRA is a common reason for 'in progress' at year-two assessments.

useCases.title: Indexer replication lag exposing evidence to single-point failure

useCases.title: Data localization enforcement — regulated-data must-stay-in-region
useCases.value: Replaces 'we think the bucket is in eu-west-1' with 'we proved every access was in-region for the full audit period'.

useCases.title: Bulk regulated-data export targeting non-adequate jurisdiction
useCases.value: Turns post-hoc 'where did our customer dataset go?' incident forensics into real-time prevention.

useCases.title: Multi-regulator breach-notification SLA tracker (24h NIS2 / 72h GDPR / 72h HIPAA)
useCases.value: Most enforcement actions against supervisory breaches (ICO, DPC, BaFin) focus on notification timeliness. This UC turns the obligation into a visible KPI instead of a post-facto audit finding.

useCases.title: Cross-regulator consistency — divergent material facts across submissions
useCases.value: Prevents the 'regulator cross-reference' problem that has escalated several prominent supervisory cases from technical fines to broader corporate sanction.

useCases.title: Key rotation attestation — KMS/HSM rotation SLA tracker
useCases.value: Gives the cryptographic custodian the ability to defend the 'our keys are rotated' claim with per-key evidence rather than a policy document.

useCases.title: Supplier attestation currency — stale SOC 2 / ISO 27001 reports for critical vendors
useCases.value: Makes vendor-risk currency a live signal rather than an annual gap report.

useCases.title: Subprocessor inventory change — notification SLA to data controllers
useCases.value: Notifications to controllers are a standard audit focus; this UC removes the manual book-keeping.

useCases.title: Fourth-party concentration risk — shared critical dependencies across vendors
useCases.value: Addresses the DORA supervisory-priorities theme that regulators ask 'who do your vendors depend on?'.

useCases.title: Vendor access telemetry — principals active outside contracted hours/geos
useCases.value: Materialises contractual access controls into operational telemetry.

useCases.title: Backup restore test evidence — RPO/RTO SLA compliance per tier
useCases.value: Makes backup testing a continuous control rather than an annual artefact.

useCases.title: Backup completeness — unprotected workloads with regulated data
useCases.value: Coverage gaps are the single most common backup finding at audit; continuous evidence eliminates surprise findings.

useCases.title: Backup repository TLS posture — aged or weak-cipher endpoints
useCases.value: Closes a gap pattern observed in DORA inspections where the backup plane had older TLS than the production plane.

useCases.title: Business-continuity rehearsal evidence — BCP/DR exercise execution logged
useCases.value: Converts a calendar item into evidence with a signed attestation per rehearsal.

useCases.title: Tabletop rehearsal evidence — IR plan exercise frequency
useCases.value: Shifts IR readiness evidence from 'we rehearse' to 'here is the per-playbook cadence record'.
